title: First pullback to VWAP in a trending stock
one_liner: Stock trends away from VWAP for 30+ min after the open, then pulls back to VWAP on lighter volume for the first time; enter with the trend on the bounce.
why_interesting: The most-cited intraday setup on trader blogs. Our older trend-pullback test used moving averages, not VWAP, and did not require 'first touch'.

title: Red-to-green / green-to-red through prior close
one_liner: A stock that opened below yesterday's close crosses back above it on 1.5-2x volume: go long (mirror for green-to-red short); stop just under prior close.
why_interesting: Prior close is a level every trader watches and is easy to compute. We tested prior-day high/low but never the prior close itself.

title: End-of-day reversal of intraday losers
one_liner: In the last 30 minutes, the day's biggest intraday losers tend to bounce (retail buying, short covering).
why_interesting: Peer-reviewed, highly significant cross-sectional effect; a different time of day from all our live setups.

title: Same half-hour continuation (Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka)
one_liner: A stock's return in a given half-hour tends to repeat at the same half-hour on following days, for weeks.
why_interesting: Published in the Journal of Finance; a new kind of signal for us (time-of-day memory per stock).

title: VWAP trend on QQQ/SPY (Zarattini-Aziz)
one_liner: Long QQQ while above VWAP, short while below, flip on each cross; reported Sharpe 2.1 (2018-2023).
why_interesting: One of the few intraday systems with a public, detailed backtest; very simple rule.

title: Lunch-hour reversal of the morning move
one_liner: Morning trends often stall and partly reverse around 12:00-13:30 as volume dries up.
why_interesting: Ties directly to the owner's question about time windows; our heat_fade_long already lives in this window.

title: Larry Williams volatility breakout
one_liner: Buy when price rises above today's open by a fixed fraction (e.g. 0.5-0.7x) of yesterday's range or ATR; mirror for shorts.
why_interesting: Classic, mechanical, easy to trade; a volatility-scaled 'move from open' trigger we have not tried.

title: Narrow initial balance -> range extension
one_liner: If the first hour's range is small versus ATR, a break of that range after 10:30 tends to keep going (trend day).
why_interesting: Crabel's contraction/expansion idea; complements NR7 (daily) with an intraday version.

title: Intraday overreaction fade (big range, small net move)
one_liner: When a stock's range today is large relative to its net move from the open, the latest swing tends to be corrected the same day.
why_interesting: Academic definition of overreaction that is a ratio, not a raw level - new to our metric set.

title: Tight flag near the high of day (intraday VCP)
one_liner: Strong stock pauses just under its high of day with shrinking bars and volume, then breaks out.
why_interesting: The 'bull flag' is the most popular momentum-trader pattern; we have never coded a contraction-then-break version.

title: 9/20 EMA cross on 5-minute bars
one_liner: Go with the trend when the fast EMA crosses the slow EMA on 5-minute bars.
why_interesting: Extremely popular; a quick baseline that tells us whether a plain crossover has any edge in our universe.

title: NR7 day + opening-range breakout
one_liner: After the narrowest daily range of 7 days, trade the break of the morning range.
why_interesting: Already in our backlog (nr7-orb); outside sources keep pointing to it as a trend-day filter.

title: First 30 minutes predicts the last 30 (index ETFs)
one_liner: If SPY is up in the first half hour, it tends to be up in the last half hour too.
why_interesting: Peer-reviewed; already in backlog (intraday-momentum-paper); reports of decay since 2018.

title: Gap fade (no-news gaps revert)
one_liner: Stocks that gap up overnight give back part of the gap during the day, especially quiet, no-catalyst gaps.
why_interesting: Our own escalation study found a short gap-fade candidate (X-gapfade-early) - still being checked.

title: Stocks-in-play 5-min opening range breakout
one_liner: Trade the first 5-minute range break only on the top-20 relative-volume names.
why_interesting: Best-documented stock ORB, but our versions after 09:50 failed (orb5, t1-orb-exits); the edge sits before 09:50.

title: Holy Grail (ADX + 20-MA pullback)
one_liner: In a strong trend (ADX > 30) buy the first pullback to the 20 MA on a break of the touch bar.
why_interesting: Close to our trend-pullback family, which failed its holdout; ADX is not yet a lab column.

title: RSI(2) extreme inside a trend (Connors)
one_liner: Buy very short-term oversold readings only when the bigger trend is up.
why_interesting: Our overbought/oversold + trend filters (obos-vwap-ma) failed; daily-bar evidence does not carry to 5-minute bars.

title: Pin bar / hammer at a key level
one_liner: Long lower wick at the day low or prior-day low signals rejection.
why_interesting: Our obos-levels setup used wicks at PDL/PDH and failed its holdout; 5-minute hammers are noisy.

title: Noise-band momentum (SPY)
one_liner: Trade SPY only when it leaves its usual intraday move band.
why_interesting: Retired here (t7, noise-band-simple); replications report the edge near zero since 2025.

title: Relative-volume breakout from consolidation
one_liner: Relative volume (vs same time of day) is the #1 stock filter for day traders.
why_interesting: Our RVOL breakout (t3) was retired; lesson so far: volume picks the stock, it does not pick the direction.
